title: How Casey Adams built a podcast into a fundraising and relationship engine from age 17
summary: Casey Adams explains how starting a podcast with no plan at 17 compounded into 450+ interviews, a funded startup and an exit. He covers shipping fast, consistency, intentional relationships, building products from real pain points, and listening as a learning edge.

principles.text: Start immediately; overthinking a launch costs months and a quick first step beats a perfect plan.
principles.quote: there was no you know overthinking there was no like true strategy or plan and I think that was one of the uh the biggest blessings at the time

principles.text: Set an aggressive volume goal with a deadline and execute against it to create momentum and access.
principles.quote: I set a goal I wanted to do 60 interviews in 90 days which is a lot and I just started being diligent about reaching out to people that I wanted to have on the show

principles.text: Cold outreach to bigger names works if you shoot your shot; a small ask can open the door.
principles.quote: I ended up getting a meeting with Gary ve when I was 17 like a five minute thing in New York City just from a cold DM on Instagram

principles.text: Long-form content compounds into intentional relationships and trust, which turn into real business opportunities like fundraising.
principles.quote: about 90% of those investors were previous guests on the podcast right so when I think about the uh the long tale of not only creating content but the compound effect of relationships but intentional relationships

principles.text: Build products from pain points you or people close to you actually experience, starting with the first small step.
principles.quote: it was just a problem that again we were dealing with that we saw through a friend and we just started with the first step

principles.text: Stay consistent by tying the medium to a bigger purpose; it is the backbone creating opportunities, not the only business.
principles.quote: it's not that the podcast is something that oh like it's my only business and the only way I make money it's it's the backbone of everything that creates so many opportunities
